name: art
tagline: Can a personal gallery be just a folder of HTML files?
description: An experiment in publishing without infrastructure. A folder of single-file HTML pages where each piece is its own little corner of the web — no CMS, no database, no build pipeline. The hypothesis: when AI handles the markup and CSS, the work matters more than the stack, and a non-developer can run their own site indefinitely.
highlights: Single-file HTML pages — readable source, no toolchain
Push to main, live in a minute on GitHub Pages
Sister project to playGround — same pattern, different audience
Built for people who paint and write, not people who deploy

name: atlas
tagline: Can AI teach you what AI just helped you build?
description: When Copilot writes the code, you get the result without the understanding. atlas closes that gap. It watches your GitHub activity, generates phone-readable lessons grounded in both your work and Microsoft Learn, and tracks what you've covered so it never repeats itself. A quiet librarian sitting between your build sessions and your understanding.
highlights: Phone-first PWA with offline reading
Lessons generated by a Foundry agent grounded in your repos
AI-managed taxonomy that grows from what you actually build
300–900 word reads with citations and 'what to learn next'

name: agentMode
tagline: Do we still need apps if a chat agent can do the job?
description: A Telegram-based personal assistant that lives on a tight Azure budget. It orders groceries by literally looking at websites with AI vision, tracks expenses, hunts cheap flights, and delivers morning briefings. The experiment: how much daily-app behaviour can be replaced by a single conversational agent — and how cheaply? 22 auto-discovered skills today, running for the price of two coffees a month.
highlights: 22 auto-discovered skills — from weather to grocery ordering
AI vision fallback: when automation breaks, the agent screenshots and navigates
Full infra-as-code, deploys with one script
Multilingual (EN, LV, RU), ~$5–10/month on Azure

name: playGround
tagline: Can kids build their own games with AI?
description: An experiment in lowering the floor for who gets to ship software. The starter shelf has four classic arcade games — Snake, Tetris, Breakout, Table Tennis — each built as a single self-contained HTML file so a kid can open the source, change it, and put it back online. The hypothesis: when AI handles the boring parts, the catalog grows with whatever kids actually want to make. Four games today. The rest is up to whoever shows up.
highlights: Workspace for young creators, not a finished games arcade
Four starter games — Snake, Tetris, Breakout, Table Tennis
Single-file source — readable, remixable, no toolchain
Catalog grows as kids ship their own ideas

name: portaBaltica
tagline: Can a public dashboard pay its own bills?
description: NauroLabs' first attempt at a self-sustaining experiment. A Bloomberg-style live dashboard for the Baltics — 30+ economic, trade, labour, energy, environmental, and maritime indicators across Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania, all from free government APIs with an AI layer on top reading the trends. The hypothesis: free raw data is a commodity, but the interpretation isn't. Free public dashboard, paid API and alerts. Goal: prove an experiment can cover its own infrastructure cost, then fund the next one.
highlights: 30+ live indicators across LV, EE, LT — economy, trade, labour, energy, property, environment
AI insights generated from live feeds, not canned summaries
Free dashboard, paid API and alerts — Moonshot v1 of the lab
All data from free public APIs: Eurostat, NordPool, ECB, Open-Meteo, data.gov.lv

name: golazo
tagline: Can gamification build better young athletes?
description: Can gamification make young footballers actually track their own training and match data? XP, levels, achievements, skill radar charts, and a collectible-style player card — built on coaching methodology from 10 football development books. Log a session, earn XP, watch the radar chart grow. Currently powering one youth midfielder's journey.
highlights: 50 levels with football ranks from Rookie to Pro
25+ drills from Coerver, Horst Wein, Dan Abrahams, UEFA methodology
Collectible player card with spider chart skills radar
4 languages: Russian, Latvian, English, Spanish

name: turgo
tagline: Can AI agents buy and sell better than humans?
description: An experiment in automating the entire buy-sell lifecycle with AI agents. The idea: you say 'sell this' with a photo, and agents handle listing creation, pricing, negotiation, and market monitoring. Testing different purchase and sales strategies to see what actually works when agents do the haggling.
highlights: Photo → AI listing → pricing → negotiation → sold
7 operational agents: moderation, analytics, anti-fraud, and more
Testing buy/sell strategies with agent-vs-agent scenarios
Multilingual: 5 UI languages, 3 Baltic countries

name: tPlan
tagline: Can AI turn a training book into a real coach?
description: Can AI read a training methodology book and act as a coach — not a tracker, not a generator, an actual coach? Feed it a calisthenics manual, it parses the progression rules, builds your plan, tracks your reps, and advances you when the book says you're ready. Turns out it follows the rules more faithfully than most humans. Now running on real training data and Phase 2 web app, with user-uploaded books planned next.
highlights: Book → program: AI parses methodology into structured plans
Auto-progression follows the book's own advancement rules
Multilingual — English, Russian, Latvian, Spanish
Phase 2 web app live; user-uploaded books planned for Phase 3

name: rosette
tagline: Where the hell do I put my sockets?
description: Upload a floor plan, get a standards-compliant electrical plan. This experiment tests whether AI can parse construction codes well enough to tell you exactly where sockets should go, how many you need per room, and which circuits need dedicated protection. Currently speaks Baltic construction codes — Latvian, Lithuanian, and Estonian.
highlights: AI analyzes floor plans to detect rooms and dimensions
Country-specific socket rules (LV, LT, EE)
SVG circuit and wiring diagrams
Possibly the world's most niche AI application

name: era
description: An experiment: can an AI agent read a country's tax code and set up the entire accounting system without a consultant? Users just throw in invoices and payments — the system figures out GL accounts, VAT, and posting rules automatically. Currently knows Latvian accounting law. World domination pending.
highlights: AI agent researches legislation and generates accounting rules
Zero settings — posting rules replace configuration
One country done, infinite ambition
Entra ID auth, Cosmos DB, full cloud-native

name: amberRepublic
tagline: What if a nation sim used real statistics?
description: Can real national statistics and AI make a governance simulation genuinely educational — and still fun? You run Latvia starting from actual 2025 data: 1.86M people, 20,000 emigrating annually, NATO border tensions, unfinished megaprojects. Every decision has second-order trade-offs you won't see coming for three turns.
highlights: Starting conditions from Latvia's actual 2025 statistics
Second-order effects — emigration causes workforce shortage causes more emigration
AI-generated events for unique playthroughs
Every decision is a painful trade-off
